subject: Proposal: rebalance hosted commit & tier caps for Velocity renewal
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@velocityhealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit sizing and rate caps questions

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Thanks for a great renewal planning call today. Velocity's usage is trending up ~45% q/q as we roll out more patient-facing features, and we need to firm up committed monthly units for 2027. A few things we want to validate before we lock terms:

- Can we shift 20% of our burst allowance into committed units for a flat monthly uplift?
- How do rate limits behave across tier boundaries? We want predictable throttling rather than unexpected 429s during batch jobs.
- Any expedited provisioning windows if we need capacity mid-term?

I attached our Q3 usage extract for context. Goal: get a proposal by the end of next week so procurement can review.

Appreciate the help — Elena

Attachments: Velocity_Usage_Report_Q3.csv (CSV, 1 file)

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@velocityhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit sizing and rate caps questions

Elena — thanks for the data. I pulled the Q3 extract and ran an initial projection; attached is a very rough commit schedule showing a phased increase into a higher monthly commit plus a small burst pocket retention. Highlights:

- Proposal: move 20% of current burst into a committed uplift of +1.2M tokens/mo starting Nov 1, with a 60-day provisioning window (provisioning sprint) to avoid cold-start throttling.
- Rate limits: we can map Velocity to the S2 tier with a hard per-route limit and a soft bank for background batch jobs. If you prefer predictable low-latency for patient-facing endpoints we recommend pinning those routes to a latency profile (will add marginal cost).
- Mid-term provisioning: we have a dedicated fast-path that can add capacity within 72 hours in emergencies (subject to commitment confirmation and a provisioning fee).

I've attached the Proposed_Commit_Schedule.pdf. Karthik / Marissa — can you confirm the mapping to commercial tiers and whether we can propose the 60-day sprint in the renewal timeline?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_Commit_Schedule.pdf (PDF, 1 file)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@velocityhealth.com>, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: rebalance hosted commit & tier caps for Velocity renewal

Elena — this aligns with what we discussed. Commercial notes: 

- We can formalize the +1.2M tokens/mo uplift as a stepped commit covering Nov–Jan at 50% uplift, then 100% thereafter, to reduce immediate cash impact.
- Pricing: stepped structure keeps the effective per-token rate within the S2 band; I'll include redline examples in the quote.
- Soft rate guard: we will enable a background batch bucket with a higher tolerance for retries; critical patient-facing endpoints should be on the pinned low-latency profile (small surcharge ~3–5%).

Marissa — can you confirm the ops handoff for the provisioning sprint (runbook, preferred blackout windows, and who will own on-call)? Markus — can legal do a quick pass on the amendment that adds the 60-day provisioning sprint clause?

Karthik Iyer
Lead Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@velocityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: rebalance hosted commit & tier caps for Velocity renewal

All — quick legal check. I reviewed the proposed amendment language for the provisioning sprint and the stepped commit ladder. Two requested edits:

1) Define "provisioning sprint" deliverables and acceptance criteria (capacity, latency profiles, and a smoke-test checklist) — helps avoid disputes on whether provisioning was completed.
2) Limit the fast-path 72-hour emergency window to three activations per rolling 12 months unless both parties agree to additional activations (keeps abuse risk managed).

If you want I can mark up the PDF and push a DocuSign envelope for the amended SOW. Happy to expedite once we lock the commercial numbers.

-Markus Klein
Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@velocityhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Finalize: provisioning sprint date and move to DocuSign

Elena — thanks for the quick turn. We're aligned on the mechanics and the two legal edits Markus suggested look reasonable from the account side. Proposed next steps:

- I'll update the Proposed_Commit_Schedule to include the provisioning sprint deliverables and acceptance checklist (will attach updated PDF).
- We will open a DocuSign envelope with the stepped-commit amendment and the SOW addendum. Please confirm if Velocity is comfortable with a Nov 1 effective date and a Nov 15–Dec 15 provisioning sprint window.

If procurement is ready I'll push the DocuSign today — once signed we'll schedule the ops runbook handoff with Marissa.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Account Manager
Redwood Inference
